action.question: How autonomous should the on-restart resume mechanism be?

questions.question: How autonomous should the on-restart resume mechanism be?

options.label: Detect + digest (safe)
options.description: On restart, scan all ~/dev projects, find interrupted sessions, write a digest + push notification with a ready `claude --resume <uuid>` command for each. You trigger the actual resume. No autonomous agents.

options.label: Auto-continue, bounded
options.description: Same scan, but also spawn a headless `claude -p --resume <uuid>` per interrupted session that runs the resume-work reconcile logic. Bounded (max N, only LAST?=ERR, skip clean/merged). Risk: autonomous edits without a human gate.

options.label: Digest now, auto-continue opt-in
options.description: Build the safe digest now; add an env-flag (off by default) that enables bounded auto-continue later once you've seen the digest behave.

transcript_tail.text: Your question could mean a couple of different things. Let me clarify before I dig in:

Here's the situation with `claude remote-control`:

**There's no native "reconnect" feature.** The server itself (`remote-control-startup.sh`) is stateless — when it restarts (crash, reboot, or the 5-min LaunchAgent re-run), it pre-creates a *fresh* session. The old session disappears from the live server list in the mobile app / claude.ai.

**But the conversation is not lost.** Every session's full transcript is persisted on disk as a `.jsonl` file under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-dir>/`. For example FamilyFund has dozens of them. So a previous session can be restored — just not through the remote-control server's UI.

Two ways to restore one:

1. **Locally in a terminal** — `cd` to the project dir and run `claude --resume` (interactive picker of past sessions) or `claude -c` (continue the most recent one). This rehydrates the exact conversation.

2. **In a fresh chat (incl. from the phone)** — use the `resume-work` skill, which lists the repo's recent/interrupted sessions + worktrees, lets you pick one, and reconstructs the goal + remaining work so you can continue it.

The remote-control server is per-directory (`mm-FamilyFund`, `mm-dev`, `mm-claude-remote-control`, etc.), so "which previous server" matters. Which project's session do you want to bring back?

Got it — you want every remote-control server to come back up *resuming its previous chats*, not starting fresh. Let me check what the `claude` CLI actually supports for that before designing a mechanism.

I dug into the actual `claude` CLI capabilities. Here's the honest constraint, then what's actually achievable.

## The hard limitation

`claude remote-control` has **no resume mechanism** for its spawned sessions. Its only flags are `--name`, `--spawn`, `--permission-mode`, `--capacity`, `--create-session-in-dir`. Resume features (`--resume`, `--continue`, `--fork-session`, `--from-pr`) exist **only for the interactive `claude` command**, not for the remote-control *server*.

The server's design is explicitly: persistent server + **ephemeral, freshly-spawned sessions**. There's no supported way to tell a remote-control server "come back up holding your previous conversations." So a true auto-resume-on-restart mechanism for the server isn't possible without the product supporting it.

## What this means in practice (better news)

Restart only actually loses the live session in two cases — **reboot or crash**. The 5-minute LaunchAgent does **not** churn sessions: `remote-control-startup.sh` keys idempotency on `pgrep -f "name $name --spawn"`, so a running server is skipped, never killed. Live sessions already survive indefinitely between intervals.

And critically: **no conversation is ever lost**. Every session's full transcript persists on disk at `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-dir>/<uuid>.jsonl` regardless of server restarts. They just have to be resumed *as a new interactive/remote session*, not reattached to the old server.

## Realistic mechanism I can build

Since the server can't auto-resume, the practical equivalent is **making the last session per project trivially resumable after a reboot/crash**:

1. **Session index** — extend `remote-control-startup.sh` to record, per directory, the most recent session UUID into `logs/last-sessions.tsv` each run. (Read-only scan of `~/.claude/projects/`.)
2. **`resume-last.sh <project>` helper** — looks up that UUID and runs `claude --resume <uuid>` in the project dir (locally), or prints the exact command. One step to bring back "the previous chat" for any server.
3. **From the phone** — document that the move is: connect to the server (fresh session) → run the `/resume-work` skill, which lists recent sessions for that repo and reconstructs the prior work. This is the only way to continue a prior chat from mobile, since the server can't reattach.

This gives you "every server's chats are restorable in one step" — which is the achievable version of what you asked, given the CLI doesn't support server-side resume.

Want me to build #1 + #2 and document #3 in the README? It's contained to this repo's script + a new helper + README, no change to the running servers' behavior.
we have the skill resume-work, can we script out a run of it, resuming all pending upon restarting sessions?

Yes — but with an important split. I read both skills' internals (`session_scan.sh`, `resume_brief.sh`, the SKILL workflows). The skill has two halves:

- **Discovery half — fully scriptable.** `session_scan.sh sessions` and `resume_brief.sh list` are read-only and deterministic. They already detect sessions that ended on an API error / interrupted (`LAST?=ERR`) and emit each one's UUID + cwd + original goal. Running this across all `~/dev` projects on restart is safe and easy.

- **Acting half — deliberately *not* safe to fully automate.** Steps 3–6 of resume-work (locate worktree, rescue, **reconcile with `main` so you don't redo already-merged work**, confirm scope) require judgement. The skill explicitly says "**Always let the user choose** — don't auto-pick." Auto-resuming *all* pending sessions on restart would spawn many headless `acceptEdits` agents that could redo merged work, collide with each other, and burn tokens with no human gate.

So there are two real designs, and the choice has safety implications:
